# Changelog — Meal planner

## 0.4.1

- Notifications: on large screens the list now opens right under the bell; on phones and tablets it stays centred on the screen. It always fits the screen: the heading stays in view and only the list scrolls.

## 0.4.0

- Week plan: a row of the week’s days; click a day to plan only that day, click it again (or open another week) for the whole week.

## 0.3.1

- The week plan opens again: it showed “This page couldn’t load” for everyone.

## 0.3.0

- A card suggests the family planner where it helps (until you connect it or close the card).

## 0.2.2

- When a member removes their DevQuake account, what they added to your things (comments, items, ticks, photos…) stays, shown as “REMOVED_…” instead of their name.

## 0.2.1

- “Back” links now return to the page you came from, with its filters and where you had scrolled to.

## 0.2.0

- The app’s card on DevQuake and its front page now show how many members use it and its totals: shared meals, planned meals, households.

0.1.0

- Plan the week’s meals for your household: breakfast, lunch, dinner and snacks, with recipes from your cookbook or meals you type in.
- Add who eats, with their portion: the servings to cook are filled in, and leftovers can be planned on purpose.
- Suggest a week for your diet, without your allergens and dislikes, no recipe twice.
- Nutrition per person and day against simple targets.
- The whole week as one shopping list: the same ingredients are added up.
- Reminders the evening before (“take the chicken out of the freezer”), by email and as a notification.
- Invite your household by link; planners change the household, everyone can add, swap and tick meals. The meals show in the family calendar when connected.
- A meal can have several parts: recipes from your Cookbook and simple items like bread or yogurt.
- Save a meal to reuse it, and make it public: others can add it to their plan, recommend it and comment, and you get a notification and the comment in your messages.
- Suggestions to connect the Cookbook and your shopping lists where they help.
